title: DACPara: A Divide-and-Conquer Parallel Approach for High-Quality Logic Rewriting in Large-Scale Circuits
problem: Logic rewriting is a time-consuming task in logic synthesis that directly impacts circuit area and delay characteristics. Existing parallel solutions suffer from runtime or quality degradation limitations when processing large-scale complex circuits.
motivation: High-quality logic rewriting is essential for optimizing synthesized circuit performance and area, making efficient parallel approaches critical for handling industrial-scale designs.
method: DACPara divides AIG nodes hierarchically by levels and employs dynamic global information to partition rewriting into three parallel processing stages. The divide-and-conquer strategy enables independent parallel execution within partitions while leveraging global circuit context to maintain result quality across the workflow.
key_novelty: Integration of dynamic global information into divide-and-conquer partitioning enables high-quality parallel logic rewriting that scales to large circuits without quality loss.
contributions: A divide-and-conquer parallel framework achieving 34.36x speedup over ABC logic rewriting
1.96x performance improvement over existing state-of-the-art CPU parallel methods with comparable quality
1.1% quality improvement over state-of-the-art GPU accelerated methods using CPU-only resources
Demonstration of scalability to 40 CPU cores on large industrial circuit benchmarks

metrics.speedup: 34.36x vs ABC, 1.96x vs CPU parallel baseline
metrics.accuracy: 1.1% quality improvement over GPU accelerated method

limitations: Limitations not discussed in abstract; scalability beyond 40 cores and applicability across different circuit classes not addressed.
primary_theme: Parallel logic rewriting for circuit synthesis optimization
